references.text: Jotham continues the same theme of acting in truth and integrity with Jerub-Beshal and his house, using the same expression 'in truth and integrity'.
Describes how the Israelites did not show kindness to the house of Jerub-Beshal (Gideon) after all the good he had done for Israel.
Explains the origin of the name Jerub-Beshal, which Gideon received after tearing down the altar of Baal.
Describes how Abimelech was made king by the men of Shechem, an action that Jotham refers to.
Uses the same expression about acting in truth and integrity (be'emet uvetamim).
Joshua urges the people to serve the Lord in integrity and truth, with similar wording.
Mentions Jerub-Beshal as another name for Gideon, father of Abimelech.
